Both stages are closed at target level relative to the exact shared foundation nodes. The independent monodromy and semistable potential-map routes are preserved in the split proposal, not counted as targets of these two stages.

nodes.title: Polynomial graph in affine space
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring k and natural numbers m,B define φ(m,B):k[X₀,…,Xₘ₋₁]→k[T] by the existing universal evaluation homomorphism, preserving coefficients and sending X_i to T^(B^i). For geometric use k is a field, m>0 and B≥2; its contravariant spectrum map is a_B:A¹_k→A^m_k.
hypotheses: k is a commutative ring; m,B are natural numbers.
proofSteps: Specialize MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom to Polynomial.C and the displayed powers of T. No new polynomial carrier is introduced.
Use evaluation on constants, variables and monomials for the normalization API; composition of evaluation gives the origin and coefficient-change formulas.
acceptance: Coordinate zero has exponent B⁰=1; the origin is preserved for B≥2.
Run all four graph tests in the reader.

sources.match: The definition is a concrete specialization of the existing universal evaluation map.
Motivates a same-field one-point curve supplier; this graph is an explicit derived replacement, not a theorem printed there.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.polynomialGraph_X
api.statement: φ(m,B)(X_i) = T^(B^i), with i numbered from zero.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.polynomialGraph_monomial
api.statement: φ(m,B)(a X^d) = C(a) T^(Σ_i d_i B^i).

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.polynomialGraph_eval_zero
api.statement: For B≥2, evaluation at T=0 after φ equals evaluation of every input coordinate at zero.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.polynomialGraph_one_variable
api.statement: For m=1, φ is precisely the existing evaluation homomorphism sending the unique variable to T, for every B.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.polynomialGraph_map
api.statement: For every commutative-ring map k→K, mapping coefficients commutes with φ(m,B), with the same m and B.

tests.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.polynomialGraph_F2_lines

tests.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.polynomialGraph_bad_base
tests.statement: Over F₂, X₁−X₀² maps to zero at B=2, and to T³−T²≠0 at B=3. The strict individual-exponent bound is essential.

tests.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.polynomialGraph_one_coordinate
tests.statement: For m=1 the variable maps to T for every B, including B=0, and the homomorphism is the usual one-variable identification.

tests.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.polynomialGraph_zero_variables
tests.statement: For m=0 constants map to constants; over a field the resulting k→k[T] is not surjective. The geometric graph-immersion statement requires m>0.

uses.how: Separates the finitely many support monomials and constructs a graph meeting the complement of a hypersurface.
Supplies a morphism from A¹ over the original field, marked at the origin, for the étale pullback.

nodes.title: Coefficients survive bounded graph substitution
nodes.statement: Let k be a commutative ring, m≥0, B≥2 and h∈k[X₀,…,Xₘ₋₁]. Assume every exponent d_i of every d∈supp(h) is <B. For every exponent vector e with all e_i<B, the coefficient of T^(Σ_i e_i B^i) in φ(m,B)(h) is exactly the coefficient of X^e in h. In particular a nonzero h has nonzero image.
hypotheses: Every support exponent and the tested exponent vector have all individual entries strictly below B.
B≥2; coefficient equality does not require a domain or characteristic zero.
proofSteps: Represent an exponent vector by its ordered list of m entries. Nat.ofDigits_eq_sum_mapIdx identifies its base-B value with Σ_i d_i B^i.
Nat.ofDigits_inj_of_len_eq gives injectivity on these bounded vectors; all lists have length m, including m=0.

Expand h as its finite sum of monomials and apply the evaluation-monomial formula. Distinct support terms have distinct powers of T, so extraction at the encoded e has exactly its original coefficient. This is a polynomial equality, not an equality of functions on k-points.
acceptance: The two terms of X₁−X₀² collide at B=2; the excluded exponent equals B.
The theorem also handles m=0 and constant h, without assuming a variable exists.

sources.locator: Defs.lean, Nat.ofDigits_inj_of_len_eq, lines 312–331; Lemmas.lean, Nat.ofDigits_eq_sum_mapIdx, lines 37–45
sources.match: These provide the existing uniqueness and positional-sum formulas. The finite-vector adapter and coefficient extraction are the new specialization.
Computes the substituted monomial; the bounded-support conclusion is derived here.

nodes.title: The graph coordinate map is surjective
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring k, m>0 and any natural number B, φ(m,B):k[X₀,…,Xₘ₋₁]→k[T] is surjective.
hypotheses: m>0; no exponent bound and no field assumption are needed.
proofSteps: The coefficient ring is in the image and X₀ maps to T because B⁰=1.
For any polynomial in T, replace T by X₀ and each coefficient by its constant multivariate polynomial. Evaluation gives the required preimage.
acceptance: For m=1 this is the usual polynomial identification.
At m=0 over a field, T is not in the image.

sources.match: The two generator formulas construct a preimage of every univariate polynomial.

nodes.title: Graph avoiding a hypersurface through the origin
nodes.statement: Let k be a commutative ring, m>0 and 0≠h∈k[X₀,…,Xₘ₋₁]. There is B≥2 strictly greater than every individual support exponent such that φ(m,B)(h)≠0 and a_B=Spec(φ(m,B)) is a closed immersion. For k a field, a_B(0)=0 and a_B⁻¹(D(h))=D(φ(m,B)(h)) is a nonempty dense open of A¹_k.
hypotheses: The nonempty/dense-open assertion uses that k is a field.
proofSteps: Choose B as at least two and one more than the maximum of the finite set of individual exponents occurring in supp(h).
Apply bounded-support-coefficients to a support exponent with nonzero coefficient.
Use graph-surjective and IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective. The origin equation follows from positive powers in every coordinate.

Over a field, k[T] is a domain and a nonzero polynomial is nonzero at the generic point. Hence its principal open is nonempty, and IsOpen.dense makes it dense. No rational point in that open is asserted.
acceptance: Over F₂ use T⁵+T⁷ to meet a hypersurface complement even when every rational line fails.
For h=T^q−T over F_q, D(h) is nonempty although it has no F_q-points.

sources.match: Turns the already surjective coordinate map into the native closed-immersion statement.

sources.locator: Proof of Corollary 5.2.7, p. 53; compare Remark 5.2.4, p. 49
sources.match: The same-field requirement motivates the derived graph-avoidance argument; this is not attributed as the paper’s displayed construction.

nodes.title: Marked component of an étale graph pullback
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, V a nonempty integral affine finite-type k-scheme, m>0, π:V→A^m_k an étale k-morphism and y∈V(k) with π(y)=0. Let U⊂V be dense open. Choose nonzero h vanishing on π(V∖U), then choose B and a_B by FC.0/avoiding-graph. In W=V×_{A^m}A¹ let C be the connected component through (y,0), with induced open scheme structure. There are maps g:C→V and q:C→A¹ and c∈C(k) with g(c)=y, q(c)=0 and πg=a_Bq. The curve C is affine, smooth of relative dimension one and geometrically integral over k, q is étale, and g⁻¹(U) is nonempty open dense.
hypotheses: V is integral, affine, finite type over k, with an étale k-chart to A^m and m>0.
y is k-rational, π(y)=0, and U is dense open.
h vanishes on the image of the complement; h need not generate its vanishing ideal.
proofSteps: The existing etale-coordinates supplier, part (c), gives nonzero h: the closure of π(V∖U) has dimension <m. Apply avoiding-graph.

Form the categorical scheme pullback W. It is affine; the projection W→A¹ is étale by base change. Since W is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation over A¹, it is finite type over k and noetherian.

The point (y,0) is k-rational. Apply rational-point-component, part (c), to obtain the open-and-closed component C, the factorization c and geometric integrality. Its closed inclusion in affine W proves affineness.
Restrict the étale projection to C. Étale is smooth of relative dimension zero; compose with A¹→Spec k, using its one-generator/no-equation submersive presentation, to obtain relative dimension one.

The nonempty étale map q is open: flatness gives Flat.generalizingMap, and local finite presentation gives isOpenMap_of_generalizingMap; this agrees with Scheme.Hom.isOpenMap for the universally open instance. Its range is a nonempty open of irreducible A¹ and meets D(φ(h)); equivalently apply the baseline open-map dense-range theorem.
A point above D(φ(h)) cannot map into V∖U by the pullback equation and h’s boundary property. Thus g⁻¹(U) is nonempty open, and is dense because C is integral.
acceptance: Run all four marked-pullback tests; in particular a point on the boundary remains marked and the component is chosen through that point.
Do not substitute the whole possibly disconnected pullback for C.

sources.locator: Corollary 5.2.7 proof, pp. 52–53; Proposition 5.3.5 proof, p. 54
sources.match: These are the smooth-chart curve uses served by this derived construction, not a claim to reproduce the separate singular local-model argument.
The imported coordinate and rational-point component contracts support the chart and integrality steps; the graph pullback and density argument are derived here.

sources.locator: Etale.lean, lines 71–112; UniversallyOpen.lean, lines 45–46 and 104–145; Smooth.lean, lines 192–214
sources.match: The baseline already supplies étale base change, étale relative dimension zero, openness and addition of smooth relative dimensions.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback.component
api.statement: For fixed V,π,y,U,h,B as in the construction, W=V×_{A^m}A¹ and w=(y,0); C is the connected component of W containing w, with its induced open subscheme structure.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback.inclusion
api.statement: j:C→W is both an open and a closed immersion. Thus C is affine and of finite type over k.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback.projections
api.statement: g=pr_V∘j and q=pr_A¹∘j satisfy π∘g=a_B∘q; s_C is either composite to Spec k.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback.point
api.statement: w factors through j to a unique k-point c of C. It satisfies g(c)=y, q(c)=0 and s_C∘c=id_Spec(k).

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback.smooth
api.statement: q is étale and s_C is smooth of relative dimension one.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback.geometricallyIntegral
api.statement: C is geometrically integral over k, by its connectedness, smoothness and rational marked point.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback.goodOpen
api.statement: q⁻¹(D(φ(m,B)(h)))⊆g⁻¹(U). The left side and hence the right side are nonempty; g⁻¹(U) is open dense.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback.chartCompatibility
api.statement: When π is the identity chart of A^m, W≅A¹, C=W, q=id and g=a_B under the categorical pullback identification.

api.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback.changeField
api.statement: After any field extension K/k, C_K is integral and connected and is the component of W_K containing c_K. Its projections are base changes of g,q, and the good open remains dense. A new coordinate chart or a new admissible B need not produce an isomorphic curve.

tests.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback_identity
tests.statement: For V=A²_k, π=id, y=0, U=A², h=1 and B=2, W=C=A¹ with q=id, g(T)=(T,T²), c=0. Both projection equations agree with the native categorical pullback.

tests.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback_boundary
tests.statement: For the same chart and U=D(X₀), h=X₀ and B=2, c=0 lies outside g⁻¹(U), while g⁻¹(U)=D(T) is nonempty dense. The construction must not require y∈U.

tests.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback_disconnected
tests.statement: Over F₃ let V=Spec k[x,z,z⁻¹] and π(x,z)=(x,z²−1−2x), an étale map to A², with y=(0,1). For h=1, B=2 and U=V the pullback has equation z²=(T+1)² with z invertible. It is the disjoint union of the two branches z=±(T+1), each isomorphic to D(T+1). The marked component is the plus branch. This tests selection by the mark, rather than use of all W.

tests.name: TauCeti.SameFieldCurves.markedPullback_origin
tests.statement: In characteristic 2, with V=A², h=X₀²X₁−X₀X₁² and B=3, C=A¹, g(T)=(T,T³), and the good open is D(T⁵+T⁷), while g(0)=0.

uses.how: Turns a positive-dimensional smooth affine neighbourhood into a marked curve meeting its chosen dense open.

uses.where: Kisin–Zhou Corollary 5.2.7 proof, p. 53; Proposition 5.3.5 proof, p. 54

nodes.title: Same-field curve through a smooth rational point
nodes.statement: Let k be any field, f:Y→Spec k a scheme over k and y:Spec k→Y a section. Suppose there is an open neighbourhood V of y on which f is smooth and U⊂Y is open with U∩V dense in V. Then there exist an affine finite-type k-scheme C, a structure map s:C→Spec k smooth of relative dimension one and geometrically integral, a k-morphism g:C→Y and c∈C(k), with g(c)=y and g⁻¹(U) nonempty open dense in C. Equivalently, it suffices that U be dense on the unique component through the smooth point y, after shrinking to that component. In particular this holds over F_q with the marked residue field exactly F_q.
hypotheses: k is a field; y is a section of Y→Spec k, not merely a closed point of arbitrary residue degree.
Y is smooth near y; U is dense on the relevant smooth component. No condition is imposed on other components or away from the chosen neighbourhood.
proofSteps: Use etale-coordinates, part (b), after shrinking inside V, to obtain integral affine V₀ through y and an étale chart π:V₀→A^m sending y to zero. Density restricts to the nonempty open V₀.
If m>0 apply marked-etale-pullback and compose g with V₀→Y. The maps are over k and the mark is unchanged.

If m=0, the connected smooth zero-dimensional affine neighbourhood through the rational point is Spec k: it is connected étale over k, and the rational component has degree one. Density forces y∈U. Take C=A¹_k, c=0 and g the constant morphism through y. This branch is a curve morphism, not an immersion.

For a finite field, the rational mark gives the identity residue-field map k→κ(c)=k→κ(y)=k. Pulling back a lisse sheaf identifies its stalk and geometric Frobenius at c with that at y, without a field-extension power. The sheaf/Frobenius theory belongs to the consumer.
acceptance: Y=Spec k and U=Y must produce A¹ with its constant map and rational zero.
For Y=A²_F₂, y=0 and U=D(X₀²X₁−X₀X₁²), use the B=3 graph and D(T⁵+T⁷).
For Y=A¹_F_q, y=0 and U=D(T^q−T), a dense good open exists even though every rational point of C=A¹ lies outside it.
If Y has a second component disjoint from U, only density on the component through y is required.
Verify c is k-rational; replacing k by F_(q^r) is not a valid output for the given y over F_q.

review.reason: Directly compared the smooth-atlas curve uses in arXiv v2, Corollary 5.2.7 proof p. 53 and Proposition 5.3.5 proof p. 54, with Poonen author-PDF Corollary 3.4, §3.3 p. 10. The corollary requires a smooth projective geometrically integral ambient variety, while these uses supply only a smooth finite-type chart. This confirms a missing justification at that citation in the inspected preprint, not a false endpoint or a defect in Poonen. The local one-point graph proof supplies the needed morphism. No verdict is made on the unavailable published article.
